Copy When to use Feature cards about inviting teammates, collaboration, sharing or multiplayer Onboarding steps like “Invite your team” where a friendly, moving scene helps When not to use Showing your real team list – the scene is decorative and loops on its own Places that need to stay completely still – use prefers-reduced-motion or a static image Installation Add Team Invite with the shadcn CLI – your project needs a components.json, see Installation in the docs – or copy the file by hand. Requires React 19. Invite your team

Bring everyone into the same workspace in seconds.

); } API reference TeamInvite Prop Type Default Description avatars [TeamInviteAvatar, TeamInviteAvatar, TeamInviteAvatar] – Required. The two connected teammates, then the one being invited – each { src, name? } with a square portrait label string – Accessible description – by default built from the names className string – Extra class on the root, e.g. for width or margins Accessibility Exposed as one image with a descriptive label built from the names; avatars, lines and cursor are hidden from screen readers Nothing in the scene is interactive Motion A 4.4 s loop with soft ease-in-out: the cursor picks up the third avatar, carries it into the dashed slot, the line draws solid and the green status dot pops in Only transforms, opacity and a stroke offset are animated – no layout work With prefers-reduced-motion it stays a still frame of the waiting state Responsive behavior Transparent background, so it sits on any light or dark surface Keeps a 3 : 2 aspect ratio and scales to the width of its container – every size is in container units Avatars are square portraits shown in white-ringed circles; photos, 3D faces or illustrations all work Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually ) has the class dark or data-theme="dark" affectUI · 54 components · 12 screens · 11 blocks · 24 illustrations · 8 motion effects affectUI Agent-ready React UI for AI products – one file each, no dependencies.
